121	Because when we engage with the inner dimension of the Torah, with the wisdom of Kabbalah, we understand
122	that in fact, as Rav Ashlag, the Baal HaSulam, writes, there is nothing out there at all.
123	What does it mean, there is nothing out there?
124	It is all a projection of the rectifications we have to make within ourselves. Everything is projected
125	outward.
126	That is, if we see an enemy out there called Amalek, then yes, we do its rectifications
127	on the screen of reality.
128	There is no way around it.
129	"If one comes to kill you, rise early and kill him first."
130	The rectifications, the easier ones and the harder ones, we do
131	within reality.
132	That is, we are not only inside.
133	But we also cannot do the rectifications only outside.
134	We must do them: to blot out the memory of Amalek
135	from within us, and to attain wholeness, clarity, and joy
136	within us.
137	That comes first, or at least alongside the external work.
138	So how can one truly be happy in such difficult days?
139	Because by the nature of things, as we said, it is very hard to be happy.
140	But the Jew is such a wonderful
141	creature,
142	who can live within nature, yet above nature.
143	That is, to be Yaakov, Yaakov's ladder, which is set on the ground, within
144	reality, with its head in the heavens.
145	Where did we first see this?
146	It is written, regarding the splitting of the Reed Sea: "And the children of Israel walked
147	on dry land in the midst of the sea."
148	What is "dry land in the midst of the sea"?
149	It comes to teach us the way in which a Jew can live.
150	Bnei Israel can live this way, as it is said of the tzaddik, "the tzaddik is the life of the worlds."
151	The life of the worlds:
152	a tzaddik can live in two worlds.
153	On the one hand, to be in this world.
154	This world is likened to a sea.
155	What does that mean?
156	A sea: when you go to the sea or the ocean, what do you see?
157	You see only the...
